chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from al-Fadl ibn Yasar from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The memorizer of the Quran and the one who acts according to it is with the senior, noble, pious angels.

key_terms.السَّفَرَهِ: The senior angels (specifically the higher ranks)
key_terms.الْحَافِظُ: The memorizer (one who has memorized the Quran)
key_terms.وَالْعَامِلُ بِهِ: And the one who acts according to it

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for memorizing and acting upon the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith elevates the status of the Quranic memorizer who also acts upon it, placing them among *al-Safar al-Kiram al-Bararah* (the noble, pious angels), a title often associated with the record-keeping angels (Kiraman Katibin). This classification underscores the Shia scholarly view that practical implementation of revelation is as crucial as memorization, granting the believer a celestial rank akin to the angels who record deeds and worship God continuously.
